newsitem.title: USA: NASD rules for Jett in Kidder Peabody arbitration.
newsitem.headline: NASD rules for Jett in Kidder Peabody arbitration.

text.p: The National Association of Securities Dealers has ruled in favor of Joseph Jett in his arbitration against Kidder, Peabody & Co, representatives for the accused bond trader said Thursday.

The NASD ruled to deny all claims by Kidder Peabody seeking a monetary award against Jett and directed that the company immediately release $1 million in Jett's account to him, according to a press release.
The remaining balance out of a total of $5.3 million in Jett's account will be held by Kidder Peabody pending a panel's decision on the issue of attorney's fees, the release said.
The parties are to appear before the panel January 23.
"This is a wonderful victory," Jett's attorney, Kenneth Warner, said in the release. "An innocent man who has been wrongly accused for nearly three years has now had his name cleared."
Kidder was owned by General Electric Co before most of its assets were sold to PaineWebber Group Inc in December 1994.
Thursday's ruling also denied Jett's claims of deferred compensation, punitive damages and a further interim award for advancement of attorneys' fees.
Kidder Peabody General Counsel John Liftin said Jett had sought $2.8 million in deferred compensation.
He said the $5.3 million in Jett's account were bonuses Jett accrued between the time he joined Kidder Peabody in July 1991 and the time he left in April 1994.
"Really what this award seems to do primarily is to deny both sides' requests for relief," Liftin said. He said the award was an interim decision rather than a final one.
Both Kidder and Jett filed for arbitration to resolve their dispute.
The arbitrated ruling does not affect fraud charges from the Securities and Exchange Commission, which in January this year accused Jett of creating phony profits to hide about $85 million in losses.
A decision from an adminsitratve law judge on the charges is pending, Liftin said.
Jett has maintained his innocence and accused Kidder Peabody of using him as a scapegoat for its losses.
